newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lebed says Russia political system near collapse.
newsitem.headline: Lebed says Russia political system near collapse.

text.p: Russian presidential hopeful Alexander Lebed predicted in interviews on arriving in France for a five-day visit on Sunday that Russia's political system would collapse within a year.
"The system which Russia's political establishment represents is condemned and rotting in place. In a year at the most it will disappear," Lebed told the daily newspaper Le Figaro.

Lebed made a strong showing in a presidential election in June last year and some opinion polls rate him as the most popular of those who hope to succeed President Boris Yeltsin. Lebed has said he expects an early election.
Lebed, who was sacked as security chief by Yeltsin last October, denied in an interview with French television that he could lead a coup to overthrow the government.
"Russia has had enough bloodshed. I stopped two wars and will do everything to avoid a coup d'etat," he said.
General Lebed warned, however, that moves to strengthen Yeltsin's powers could push the Russian people to the streets.
"I want to avoid this. In Russia, the people take a long time to rise but when they do it takes a lot of time and a lot of blood to stop it," he said.

Lebed said the Russian army "didn't count any longer" and the government had given real military muscle to interior ministry troops who were "much better equipped, armed and paid...they make up half the military system today".
The Russian officer, who is due to meet Bank of France officials and French business leaders, said, however, that Western businessmen were right to invest in Russia.
"Russia is a gigantic potential market. The first one who comes will be the best served -- but it is not without risks," he said.

General Lebed was limping when he arrived and aides said he was suffering from an in-grown toenail which forced him to cancel planned visits to Napoleon's tomb and the French army museum. Instead, he was taken to the Eiffel Tower.
French radio said he would be treated later by the doctor of the Paris St-Germain football team.
He will meet the presidents of the National Assembly and the Senate as well as Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin.
He will also meet several prominent members of the ruling Rally for the Republic (RPR) Gaullist party, including Senator Philippe de Gaulle, son of former president Charles de Gaulle.
